orbit_identification.argument: The prior standard G26 invariant ring is C[u6,u12,u18]. Every nonzero common zero has nonzero u18 and can be scaled to the T value. Fibers of a finite-group invariant quotient are single group orbits. Therefore these 72 rays are the projective G26/Clifford T orbit, independently of numerical orbit counting.

physical_boundary: A constructed scalar effective potential, not an action uniquely derived from W33.
Degree-12 and degree-24 interactions are nonrenormalizable in four dimensions; a cutoff or UV mechanism is required.
Positive coefficients and radius are external inputs; angular vacuum location is independent of their values, masses are not.
The U(1) phase is flat unless gauged or lifted; no CP/time orientation is selected.
A classical scalar vacuum is not a prepared qutrit state or a fault-tolerant magic factory.
The chosen zero of V is not a prediction for the cosmological constant; additive vacuum energy and quantum corrections are unconstrained.

potential.Hessian_scope: Euclidean real kinetic coordinates of the standard unitary representation; coefficients are not physical predictions
potential.minimizers: 72 projective rays at norm r0; each retains a common U(1) phase
potential.parameters: lambda,alpha,beta,r0 > 0 (appropriate powers of a cutoff for dimensionful fields)
potential.proof: All summands are nonnegative and T has u6=u12=0. The reduced complete intersection consists of 72 rays. Radial square fixes the norm. The angular Hessian is 2 Re(J^dag diag(alpha,beta) J), positive on the projective tangent; no global numerical optimization is used.
